observations: Photo 0 shows a large cardboard shipping box for a Sharp Digital Multifunctional System.
The brand 'SHARP' is printed prominently on the front of the box.
A white identification label on the left side of the box shows 'BP-20M2', with the following characters obscured by a white plastic packing strap.
The box is sealed with two vertical white plastic straps.
The actual photocopier is not visible in the photo.
Text on the box confirms it is a 'DIGITAL MULTIFUNCTIONAL SYSTEM' in multiple languages.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows the Sharp brand and the start of the model number on the box label.
Photo 0 box text reads 'DIGITAL MULTIFUNCTIONAL SYSTEM'.

risks.risk: The box may be empty or contain a different, older, or damaged unit.
risks.proof: A photo of the actual machine outside of the box.

risks.risk: The machine may not power on or may have internal mechanical faults.
risks.proof: A video of the machine powering on and printing a test page.

risks.risk: The internal page counter (meter) may be very high, indicating the machine is near the end of its service life.
risks.proof: A photo of the printed status page or the digital counter on the machine's display.

proof_requests: Photo of the actual machine outside of the box.
Photo of the model and serial number plate on the back or side of the machine.
A photo of the total page count (meter reading) from the machine's display or a printed status sheet.
A video showing the machine performing a copy or print operation.
response.reason: Only the shipping box is shown. For high-value office equipment, the actual unit must be inspected to verify its existence, physical condition, and usage history (page count) before a price can be determined.
